A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CWMI research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and references support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on four datasets using U-Net and Attention U-Net, together with ablations, qualitative examples, and timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the same datasets, revised quantitative comparisons, and additional VMUNet and ablation experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed loss retains complex steerable decomposition, covariance-based mutual-information estimation, and combination with cross-entropy. VMUNet is an additional evaluation architecture; magnitude-only and phase-only variants are ablation controls.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same segmentation tasks on SNEMI3D, GlaS, DRIVE, and MASS ROAD. The added architecture and loss-component experiments do not introduce another dataset, population, or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds Sensitive loss, attributed to Tang et al. (2025), alongside the eleven existing baseline losses in Table 1 across all four datasets. The original comparators remain. Newly cited neural mutual-information estimators are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a SNEMI3D evaluation using VMUNet trained for 100 epochs; the existing U-Net and Attention U-Net experiments retain their 50-epoch setting. It also introduces lambda settings of 0.1, 0.5, and 0.9 for sensitivity testing. Existing datasets, preprocessing, metrics, and optimizer settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the examination of CWMI's components: Table 4 compares magnitude-only, phase-only, real-only, and full complex representations, while Table 5 adds cross-entropy-weight sensitivity. These test component attribution and loss balancing beyond v1's real-versus-complex comparison. Existing metric, decomposition, layer, and timing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-fold cross-validation and plus/minus values without specifying repetitions. v2 specifies at least two repeated three-fold cross-validations and adds Student's t-test significance annotations, defining the reported p-value as the maximum across baseline comparisons. This substantially expands statistical reporting without establishing how many repetitions v1 used.

E6.justification: Table 1 extensively revises reported means and dispersions; for example, GlaS/U-Net CE mIoU changes from 0.808±0.009 to 0.637±0.204. v2 adds Sensitive-loss results, VMUNet results, and component and lambda ablation entries. Original distance-metric, decomposition, layer, and timing results are retained. These are changes in reported evidence, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The wavelet filters, mutual-information approximation, combined loss, and computational-complexity derivation remain unchanged. v2 explicitly writes the standard Hermitian covariance and cross-covariance formulas already invoked in v1 and omits the entropy identity; these clarify existing mathematics without changing assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: a multiscale complex-wavelet mutual-information loss improving segmentation accuracy and structural preservation with limited overhead. Additional experiments support this existing positioning without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that magnitude supports clustering quality, phase alone is insufficient, and the full representation balances metrics. It also interprets lambda sensitivity and explains cross-entropy's role in distinguishing inverted label assignments. The stated need to validate multiclass and 3D extensions remains.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository, and the SNEMI3D reference gains a dataset URL. v2 explicitly attributes the unchanged N, K, and lambda choices to ablations and spells out complex covariance calculations. Existing hardware and core implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MINE, Deep InfoMax, VMUNet, MedMamba, and Sensitive loss. It briefly positions the chosen mutual-information estimator against neural estimators on computational overhead. The broader related-work narrative and wavelet-loss novelty claim remain.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections and expands the estimator, experimental, and ablation discussions. It adds affiliation, proceedings information, and acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most existing prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds VMUNet and component-ablation tables, expands the sensitivity table with lambda rows, and adds baseline rows and significance annotations to Table 1. All six figure images are retained, with several relocated. The two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful architecture and ablation evidence and explicit statistical testing, but introduces unresolved reporting problems. Unlike v1, Table 1 repeats complete Attention U-Net metric rows for eleven baselines between GlaS and MASS ROAD. Section 4.2 also overstates significance relative to the table annotations, including SNEMI3D Attention U-Net HD. These issues undermine central comparisons, preventing a reliable judgment that the added evidence produces a net quality improvement.
